slug: 2017-01-01 AU - Report on the Status of Civil Registration and Vital Statistics in Africa
note: A continental summary of the October 2016 APAI-CRVS monitoring round, reported as counts of countries. Burundi is named only in the annex: scored 50-64% on legal framework and 65-79% on infrastructure and resources, and the footnotes say Burundi lacks data on digitization, on planning and coordination, on the registration process, on vital statistics and on the overall score. Nothing is stated about how Burundi's offices record events.

The commercial code: its one passage with a study term (article 62) makes a change in a trader's civil status a matter for a further entry in the trade register. It says nothing of civil registration; the trade register is out of scope.

It is classed archive because the document describes keying, in 2026, the registers of events of 2025; it does not say the event is entered when registered, nor that the keying is routine for each new event. facts.fact: The Government of Burundi's own report states that ordinary registration continues as usual although the civil-status services 'currently' suffer from a lack of computerised data; the report gives no date for the statement, so its date of receipt by the UN, 3 December 2021, is used rather than its 2025 publication date.
facts.system: services d'état civil

systems.platform: none stated; the report says the services lack computerised data
systems.tiers: the civil-status office of the mother's domicile, where a birth is declared within fifteen days; provincial civil-status controllers

note: The value 'paper' is the nearest closed value to the report's words (a lack of computerised data); the report does not use the word paper. Also stated, with no aspect to carry it: a national ad hoc steering committee chaired by the First Vice-President, functional since 2014; distance from civil-status offices listed first among causes of non-registration; 84% of under-fives registered (EDS 2016-2017), from 54% in Kirundo to 94% in Gitega.

A note on the Merankabandi social-protection MIS (CORE-MIS on openIMIS, hosted at SETIC) and the planned unified social registry, none of which falls in the typology. It says only that CORE-MIS supports integration with third-party systems such as ID databases; no civil registration or identity system is named for Burundi.

The one passage with a study term is a list of recommendations on national ID, one of which is to resolve overlapping institutional arrangements on identity 'between the National Registration Bureau and the Department of Civil registration' (names the passage does not otherwise explain for Burundi). No system is described and nothing is said of how offices register events.

The health-informatics plan 2020-2024: its one passage with a study term plans an intersectoral collaboration forum between the health ministry and bodies including 'Ministère de l'Intérieur/CRVS'. A planned forum only; no civil registration system, link or notification is described.

facts.fact: A director at the Ministry of the Interior states that Rumonge is the 12th commune of Burundi whose civil status service is digitalised, and that the process will continue in other communes; no total of communes or offices is given.

facts.fact: The project launched at Rumonge on 19 July 2024 is for the digital registration of births and deaths at the commune's civil status service, at the commune seat and in its zones, so that each child born is registered directly, as FVS-Amade and the Ministry of the Interior state.
facts.system: enregistrement numérique à l'Etat-civil

facts.fact: The local NGO FVS-Amade is to give Rumonge commune's civil status service computers, tablets, solar panels and routers and to train its agents, in a project lasting one year; participants at the launch doubted the commune could keep digital registration going without that support, and no domestic budget is named.
facts.system: enregistrement numérique à l'Etat-civil

facts.fact: The communal administrator of Rumonge states that until this project births and deaths in the commune were registered by hand in registers.
